Coupang (CPNG) stock rose 12.0% on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 1.6%. The advance came the day after the e-commerce company reported third-quarter results on November 3, during a session where all five companies on its Trefis peer list also climbed. So what did Coupang's quarter show?

Coupang Beat Sales Estimates With Mixed Per-Share Results

Coupang's revenue reached $9.96 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, clearing the analysts' consensus estimate of $9.76 billion. Sales grew 7.5% from a year earlier. Measured at constant exchange rates, management put growth at 11%, exceeding the 8% to 9% range it had guided to.

Against estimates, the per-share results proved mixed. Coupang recorded $248 million in costs during the quarter from a July fire at one of its fulfillment centers. Including the fire, the company posted a loss of $0.28 per share. Excluding it, the loss was about $0.18 per share. That missed the $0.09 loss in our earnings calendar's consensus but beat the Zacks consensus of a $0.23 loss.

Management also discussed Product Commerce, its main retail business. The segment generated an adjusted EBITDA margin of 4.6%, down about 420 basis points from a year earlier. Management tied part of the decline to last year's data incident, after which some WOW members left. Management believes the third quarter was the low point for that margin and expects it to return to about pre-incident levels by the middle of 2027.

Did Coupang Rise Alone Or With Other Retailers?

Coupang climbed with other retailers, advancing further than any of its five Trefis peers. Etsy gained 7.1% and Amazon added 6.1% that session, and XLY, the SPDR fund for consumer discretionary stocks, rose 4.3%.

Where Does Coupang Stock Stand Now?

Such a large advance is rare for Coupang. Only one other session in the previous 365 days brought a gain at least this big: a 14.1% rise on June 11, 2026.

The stock remains far below where it traded a year ago. Coupang stock lost 46.9% over the twelve months to November 4, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 14.9%. Its highest close during that period was $32.13 on November 4, 2025, and its lowest was $13.75 on September 28, 2026. The stock has climbed back part of the way over the past month, returning 18.2% from October 6 to November 4 while the S&P 500 lost 1.6%.

Coupang's next report will cover the fourth quarter of 2026. Management expects revenue growth of 13% to 14% at constant exchange rates for that quarter, and that growth rate is the number to watch.

Symbotic SYM, which specializes in AI-powered warehouse automation, combining robotic systems with proprietary software to orchestrate inventory movement, routing and fulfillment, recently expanded its commercial partnership with Walmart WMT to introduce advanced automation capabilities across 25 regional distribution centers in the United States.

The multiyear agreement involves an initial spending commitment of approximately $6 billion, covering projects at multiple facilities. Through this arrangement, Symbotic will deploy additional AI-driven technologies to improve operational efficiency, expand distribution capabilities and support Walmart's global growth initiatives.

According to Symbotic chairman and CEO Rick Cohen, the relationship with Walmart has evolved considerably since its inception more than a decade ago, progressing from a single-product offering to a comprehensive supply chain automation solution.

Symbotic's technology portfolio includes its BreakPack individual-item picking system and SymMicro micro-fulfillment solution, designed to support e-commerce operations. These offerings rely on proprietary AI-powered software that coordinates and optimizes the daily movement of millions of product cases.

The enhanced automation infrastructure is expected to strengthen upstream e-commerce inventory management, increase storage capacity and streamline product movement. These improvements should enable Walmart to expand its merchandise selection, accelerate fulfillment and ensure more consistent inventory replenishment throughout the distribution network.

Symbotic stands to benefit directly from the expanded Walmart agreement through greater revenue visibility, a stronger order pipeline and increased deployment opportunities. The agreement also lets Symbotic expand adoption of the AI-powered automation solutions across 25 Walmart regional distribution centers in the United States, strengthening its presence in one of the world's largest retail supply chains. Wider deployment of its integrated technologies, including BreakPack and SymMicro, could create additional opportunities for software integration, system upgrades and ongoing customer support.

Moreover, the agreement opens avenues for further expansion across Walmart's international supply chain network, potentially broadening Symbotic's geographic reach and addressable market. The extended partnership reinforces Symbotic's competitive position in warehouse automation while providing opportunities to scale operations, improve resource utilization and generate additional long-term business.

Grubhub parent Wonder files confidentially to go public in the US

Investing.com -- Wonder Group Inc. has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering of its Class A common stock, setting the stage for one of the food-tech sector's most anticipated public debuts. While the offering size and price range remain undecided pending regulatory review, the move follows a July financing round that secured $650 million and valued the startup at $9 billion pre-money.

Founded by serial entrepreneur Marc Lore, the New York-based platform operates multi-brand shared kitchens alongside high-profile delivery and meal-prep acquisitions. The planned float tests Wall Street's appetite for a unified food ecosystem that aims to challenge incumbents by controlling everything from culinary preparation to final delivery.

Lore, who previously sold Jet.com to Walmart for more than $3 billion, has moved aggressively to streamline the company's sprawling footprint ahead of the prospective listing. Wonder completed its $650 million acquisition of Grubhub from Just Eat Takeaway.com NV last year, slashing 23% of the delivery unit's staff to integrate operations while eliminating restaurant fees on orders over $50 to defend market share against DoorDash Inc. and Uber Technologies Inc.

To sharpen its balance sheet and core focus, the company also reached an agreement to divest Grubhub's campus dining operations to rival DoorDash for $300 million. Meanwhile, Wonder overhauled meal kit provider Blue Apron, abandoning its legacy subscription model in favor of a-la-carte prepared meals designed to capture a broader consumer demographic.

The confidential filing signals Wonder's intent to test public markets as it absorbs these acquisitions and accelerates unit growth. Investors will likely scrutinize whether the group's shared-kitchen economics and restructured assets can deliver sustainable profitability against entrenched food delivery rivals.

Could You Have Seen The Run In eBay Stock Coming?

eBay (EBAY) stock returned 55.2% in the year to November 4, 2026, against 14.9% for the S&P 500. eBay's sales growth picked up sharply over those months. On the October 28, 2026 call, management pointed to consumers selling to each other and to the categories it chose to focus on, such as collectibles, motors and fashion. So when did that growth first show up where you could have seen it?

eBay Showed The First Signs In February 2025

That first sign arrived on eBay's February 26, 2025 call for the fourth quarter of 2024. Management said its focus category volume grew 5% in 2024, while gross merchandise volume, the value of goods sold across the whole marketplace, grew by just over 1%. During the same call, management described an overhaul of selling between consumers in the U.K., its second-largest market. Those are the same two areas management pointed to in October 2026. Yet eBay's revenue had grown only 0.7% in the quarter ended December 2024, so the sign was easy to dismiss.

In 2025, eBay's revenue growth picked up in each quarter, moving from 1.1% in the quarter ended March to 6.1% in the quarter ended June. On October 30, 2025, eBay filed its report for the quarter ended September with revenue up 9.5% from a year earlier. That filing arrived days before the twelve months measured here began.

eBay stock was already rising by then, gaining 21.5% in the six months before November 3, 2025. So the signs could be read in public. Anyone who waited for the September quarter's filing bought late in that rise, but still before the run measured here began.

eBay's Revenue Growth More Than Tripled In A Year

eBay's revenue grew 15.7% in the four quarters to September 2026, against 4.4% in the four quarters before. Over the run, eBay stock beat three of its peers: Walmart returned 27.4%, Amazon 6.7% and MercadoLibre fell 24.5%.

During the October 28, 2026 call, management said its focus categories, consumer-to-consumer selling and recommerce, the resale of used goods, together grew merchandise volume by about 20% in the third quarter. Those businesses now make up 72% of eBay's merchandise volume, excluding Depop, the consumer-to-consumer fashion marketplace eBay finished buying on July 30, 2026. Management singled out two of those three areas in February 2025.

Are eBay's Focus Categories Still Growing Faster Today?

Yes. Management said focus category volume grew 24% in the third quarter of 2026, outpacing the rest of the marketplace by 19 percentage points. Collectibles, motors, fashion and refurbished goods all added to growth.

What Could Derail Amazon Stock?

Amazon.com (AMZN) stock returned 6.7% over the year to November 4, 2026, against 14.9% for the S&P 500. Holders waiting for the stock to catch up may be counting on AWS, Amazon's cloud business, which grew at its fastest pace in nearly five years in the third quarter. Yet on the October 29 call, management also pointed to pressure on the cloud's margins. Where does that pressure come from?

Amazon Says Its AI Sales Carry Lower Margins

The pressure comes from the AI business inside AWS. Asked about AWS margins over the next two years on the October 29 call, management said the outsized growth of AI puts margin pressure on the business as a whole, because AI earns lower margins. AI is also growing faster than the rest. Management said AI revenue was growing at triple digits from a year earlier, while AWS as a whole grew 39.3% in the third quarter.

On the same call, management named a second squeeze from component pricing headwinds, which it said it cannot predict. It also expects AWS margins to move around, partly with how much the company is investing at the time. Amazon's cash capital spending reached $75.9 billion in the third quarter, mostly for AWS and AI.

How Much Of Amazon's Profit Comes From AWS?

Close to two-thirds came from the cloud unit in the third quarter. AWS earned $17.8 billion of Amazon's $28.1 billion in operating income. It produced that income on $46 billion of revenue, under a quarter of the company's $201.9 billion total, so a squeeze on AWS margins lands on most of Amazon's profit.

AWS margins could go either way from here as AI grows. On one side, AWS posted a 38.7% operating margin in the third quarter, and management said its AI margins are rapidly improving, well ahead of where its core cloud business stood at a similar stage. On the other, management gives no guidance on AWS margins. It expects to spend meaningfully more in 2027 than the roughly $220 billion of cash capital spending it expects for 2026, the majority for AWS.

Investors pay a little more for Amazon's sales than for the market's. The stock trades at 3.6 times sales, against 3.2 for the S&P 500. Since late 2016, that multiple has ranged from 1.7 at the end of 2022 to 4.5 in September 2020. On November 4, the stock closed 6.3% below its high of the past year, set on August 3. The November 4 close capped a 6.1% one-day gain, as big tech stocks rallied after the midterm election results.
